method: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from CARI Guidelines, Nephrology (Wiley) 'CARI Guidelines Commentary on the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Glomerular Diseases' (published 16 September 2025). Every claim is a paraphrase backed by anchors (scripts/anchor.py): verify.py --source re-finds each anchored span in a fresh copy of the source, checks the claim's numbers against it and rejects copying. LICENCE: CC BY-NC 4.0 (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <license> element for PMC12439324). The source's words are NOT reproduced here.

claims.claim: **Report kidney biopsies with a validated international scoring system** (for lupus nephritis, the ISN/RPS classification). Biopsy remains key in glomerular disease when the cause is not clear.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Nephrology (Wiley), 'CARI Guidelines Commentary on the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Glomerular Diseases', published 16 September 2025, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12439324, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **With marked proteinuria in adults, prefer a timed urine collection** over a random spot sample to measure protein: it is more accurate and varies less.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Nephrology (Wiley), 'CARI Guidelines Commentary on the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Glomerular Diseases', published 16 September 2025, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12439324, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Creatinine-based eGFR overestimates true GFR** in nephrotic syndrome with low albumin, and CKD-EPI is unvalidated in Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander and Māori people.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Nephrology (Wiley), 'CARI Guidelines Commentary on the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Glomerular Diseases', published 16 September 2025, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12439324, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Give people starting immunosuppression a third primary COVID vaccine dose** (ATAGI), ideally more than 2 weeks before treatment starts. This covers high-dose steroids (> 20 mg/day for > 14 days), mycophenolate, azathioprine, calcineurin inhibitors, cyclophosphamide and anti-CD20 agents.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Nephrology (Wiley), 'CARI Guidelines Commentary on the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Glomerular Diseases', published 16 September 2025, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12439324, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Do not wait for a biopsy or positive serology before treating AAV,** especially when kidney function is falling fast.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Nephrology (Wiley), 'CARI Guidelines Commentary on the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Glomerular Diseases', published 16 September 2025, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12439324, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Do not base treatment decisions on ANCA titres alone:** positivity or rising titres do not reliably predict relapse. Loss of PR3-ANCA after rituximab goes with longer remission; turning from negative to positive goes with higher relapse risk.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Nephrology (Wiley), 'CARI Guidelines Commentary on the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Glomerular Diseases', published 16 September 2025, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12439324, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Induce remission with a glucocorticoid plus cyclophosphamide or rituximab.** Prefer rituximab in children and adolescents, pre-menopausal women, men worried about fertility, older adults, relapsing disease and PR3-ANCA positive disease.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Nephrology (Wiley), 'CARI Guidelines Commentary on the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Glomerular Diseases', published 16 September 2025, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12439324, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **With severe disease (serum creatinine > 354 μmol/L), prefer glucocorticoid plus cyclophosphamide.** IV cyclophosphamide suits a moderate cumulative dose, low white cell count or poor adherence, where an infusion centre is close.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Nephrology (Wiley), 'CARI Guidelines Commentary on the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Glomerular Diseases', published 16 September 2025, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12439324, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Give pneumocystis prophylaxis for the whole cyclophosphamide course, or for 6 months after rituximab,** and monitor IgG for hypogammaglobulinaemia.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Nephrology (Wiley), 'CARI Guidelines Commentary on the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Glomerular Diseases', published 16 September 2025, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12439324, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Use reduced-dose steroids:** with cyclophosphamide, bring prednisolone down to 5 mg/day within 6 months; with rituximab, stop it within 6 months. **Avacopan** can spare or replace glucocorticoids and has been PBS-listed for ANCA vasculitis since October 2024.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Nephrology (Wiley), 'CARI Guidelines Commentary on the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Glomerular Diseases', published 16 September 2025, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12439324, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Reserve plasma exchange for specific cases:** diffuse alveolar haemorrhage, creatinine > 5.7 mg/dL (500 μmol/L) needing dialysis, rapidly rising creatinine, or combined AAV and anti-GBM disease.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Nephrology (Wiley), 'CARI Guidelines Commentary on the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Glomerular Diseases', published 16 September 2025, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12439324, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **In anti-GBM plus ANCA double-positive disease, maintain as for ANCA vasculitis.**
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Nephrology (Wiley), 'CARI Guidelines Commentary on the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Glomerular Diseases', published 16 September 2025, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12439324, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Proteinuria does not reliably track how severe the nephritis is,** so assess clinical and laboratory findings together. Base the decision to treat class III/IV disease on the biopsy.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Nephrology (Wiley), 'CARI Guidelines Commentary on the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Glomerular Diseases', published 16 September 2025, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12439324, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Hydroxychloroquine for every patient.** First-line induction is a corticosteroid with a mycophenolic acid analogue (MPAA) or low-dose IV cyclophosphamide, starting with IV glucocorticoid pulses then a lower starting dose tapered quickly.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Nephrology (Wiley), 'CARI Guidelines Commentary on the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Glomerular Diseases', published 16 September 2025, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12439324, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Choose between MPAA and low-dose cyclophosphamide on availability, adherence, age, severity, ethnicity and past treatment:** efficacy is similar and low-dose cyclophosphamide has fewer adverse events. Standard-dose IV cyclophosphamide may help severe disease (AKI, cellular crescents, fibrinoid necrosis).
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Nephrology (Wiley), 'CARI Guidelines Commentary on the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Glomerular Diseases', published 16 September 2025, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12439324, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Alternatives:** MPAA with a calcineurin inhibitor. ⚠️ Belimumab (for lupus nephritis) and voclosporin (which helps when eGFR > 45 mL/min/1.73 m2, with MPAA) are **not available in Australia or New Zealand**.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Nephrology (Wiley), 'CARI Guidelines Commentary on the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Glomerular Diseases', published 16 September 2025, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12439324, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Maintain with low-dose glucocorticoid plus MPAA;** azathioprine is second line, then a calcineurin inhibitor or mizoribine. Continue for at least 36 months, stopping glucocorticoids after 12 months in complete remission.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Nephrology (Wiley), 'CARI Guidelines Commentary on the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Glomerular Diseases', published 16 September 2025, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12439324, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Rituximab is an option for refractory disease or when steroids must be minimised.** Class V treatment depends on proteinuria, with RAAS blockade plus immunosuppression for nephrotic syndrome.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Nephrology (Wiley), 'CARI Guidelines Commentary on the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Glomerular Diseases', published 16 September 2025, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12439324, retrieved 2026-09-23
